finding: Negative WTI prints on 2020-04-20 in three series (not one, as the context doc states).
evidence: DCOILWTICO -36.98; CL1 -37.63; USCRWTIC -37.63. Wednesday 2020-04-22 is positive in all (FRED 13.64, CL1 13.78).
classification: potentially genuine market event (corroborated by 3 series; May-2020 contract expiry and storage squeeze)
why_it_matters: Log returns are undefined for prices <= 0; the hedged-return distribution around this week drives the WTI 1% tail.
risk_if_ignored: A fallback day rule that reaches back to Mon/Tue, or any daily-frequency step, would crash or silently drop the week; holding the expiring May contract into expiry would create an artificial futures loss.
recommended_action: Keep the print in raw data; never take logs of nonpositive prices; make Stage-2 sampling assert price>0; ensure the roll rule has left CLK20 before 2020-04-20.
verification: Unit test: every price entering a log is >0; print the weekly rows 2020-04-08..2020-05-06 for review.

finding: FRED WTI spot is blank on many trading days, concentrated in 1994-2006.
evidence: 1117 blank rows; 164 of 1922 Wednesdays missing (8.5%); 161 missing to Jun-2023; CL1 traded on 705 of the blank days. Context doc reports 99.0% weekly spot coverage (19 missing weeks).
classification: unresolved (cannot tell from the file whether the gaps exist at FRED/EIA or arose in the pull; live re-download blocked in this environment)
why_it_matters: Every missing spot Wednesday removes a hedged-return observation or forces a substitute day; 1994-2006 is ~1/3 of the replication sample.
risk_if_ignored: Silent loss of ~8% of weeks, or a substitute-day rule applied far more often than assumed, which changes the sample relative to the paper (1,728 weeks).
recommended_action: Re-download DCOILWTICO from FRED and RWTC from EIA and diff against this file before Stage 2; if gaps are real, apply a documented common-date fallback and report how many weeks use it.
verification: Diff report: count of dates where fresh download has a value and this file is blank (target 0).

finding: FRED spot sits persistently above CL1 from 2024 onward, peaking ~6% in Oct-2026; before 2024 the ratio is ~1.000 even in the steep 2022 backwardation.
classification: unresolved (possible change in EIA/LSEG spot assessment method, or a genuine physical premium; not determinable from raw files)
why_it_matters: The H1 extension (2023-2026) depends on spot-futures basis; a level shift that varies over time adds basis noise, which favours estimated (OLS) hedges over naive.
risk_if_ignored: A source artifact could be misread as evidence that the naive hedge stops working after 2023.
recommended_action: Check EIA notes for RWTC methodology changes; in Stage 2 report WTI results for 2023-2026 with FRED spot and, as sensitivity, with CL1-implied spot.
verification: Weekly basis volatility by year before/after 2024; result tables under both spot definitions.

finding: FRED spot printed 15-30% below CL1 for several days at end-March 2020, including Wednesday 2020-03-25.
classification: potentially genuine market event (physical Cushing dislocation during COVID storage crisis), but unconfirmed
why_it_matters: A single week of extreme basis sits in the March-2020 stress window and can dominate tail estimates for a 52-week window.
risk_if_ignored: If it is a reporting artifact, it inflates WTI basis risk and penalises the naive hedge in 2020-21.
recommended_action: Keep; flag the week; run a sensitivity with the week excluded. The daily screen shows the whole 2020-03-19..2020-03-31 window has FRED moves not matched by CL1 (see supporting/daily_outlier_screen.csv).
verification: Compare HE with/without the flagged week in Stage 2/3.

finding: Bloomberg 'WTI Cushing spot' equals CL1 exactly on most days and starts only in 2017.
evidence: share exactly equal to CL1 = 85.9%; median ratio 1.0; differs mainly around CL1 roll dates.
classification: verified fact (exact equality); interpretation: series is front-month futures-based, not an independent physical spot
why_it_matters: Using it as spot would make spot and futures nearly the same series.
risk_if_ignored: Basis risk would be ~0 by construction, so every hedge looks near-perfect and the naive hedge wins trivially.
recommended_action: Do not use USCRWTIC as the spot leg; keep it as a cross-check only.
verification: Reported equality share in cross_source_comparison.csv.

finding: FRED ends on Tuesday 2026-11-03; the last Wednesday with a FRED WTI price is 2026-10-28.
evidence: last valid 2026-11-03; context doc says last common Wednesday is 2026-11-04 (true only under a fallback-day rule).
classification: verified fact
why_it_matters: Defines the end of the WTI sample.
risk_if_ignored: Off-by-one week in sample end or a silent fallback.
recommended_action: Decide sample end explicitly (2026-10-28 strict Wednesday, or 2026-11-04 with fallback).
verification: Assert last sample date in Stage 2.

finding: CME pound futures are quoted in US cents per pound; spot is in dollars.
evidence: median BP1/GBPUSD = 99.9557 (p1 98.6986, p99 100.3845); after /100 median = 0.9996. Deviation from 1 has the sign implied by interest-rate parity (futures below spot when UK rates > US rates, e.g. 1990; above in 2000, 2006 and 2016-2025 when US rates were at or above UK rates; checked by eye).
classification: verified (unit convention); deviation pattern is a reasonable interpretation (carry)
why_it_matters: Log returns are unit-free, so the /100 matters for levels, basis, and any ratio-based check, not for returns.
risk_if_ignored: Basis computed in levels would be ~99 dollars, corrupting basis-risk splits.
recommended_action: Divide BP1-3 by 100 in Stage 2 processing (never in raw files).
verification: Median processed ratio in [0.98, 1.02].

finding: BP3 has multi-week gaps (39 days to 1996-07-26, 30 days to 1990-04-18); the BP calendar lists serial months only from 2017, and generics skip them.
evidence: roll test: cycle months 0.946 (3d/5x: 0.973); off-cycle months 0.026 (3d/5x: 0.247)
classification: potentially genuine (illiquid third contract); serial-month skipping verified statistically
why_it_matters: BP3 is needed only for contract mapping; mapping with serial months included would mis-identify contracts after 2017.
risk_if_ignored: Wrong contract identified at rolls => spurious futures returns.
recommended_action: Filter BP calendar to H/M/U/Z before mapping; do not use BP3 levels in analysis.
verification: Stage 2 mapping test: implied roll dates match spread jumps.

finding: Big-SP generics equal E-mini generics to the cent on many days, rising to ~98% in 2021Q2-Q3.
evidence: share SP1==ES1: 1997-2020 25.8%; 2021 82.8%. Expiry handling differs: 2021-06-18 SP1 4153.5 = ES2 4153.5 while ES1 4187.25 (final settlement of expiring contract). SP calendar LTD is Thursday (2021-06-17), ES LTD Friday.
classification: verified equality; interpretation: CME settled SP off ES as SP liquidity disappeared (not a data error)
why_it_matters: The SP-to-ES switch point barely changes price levels, but the two generics roll on different days.
risk_if_ignored: A transition week computed as ln(ES1_t) - ln(SP1_t-1) mixes contracts and can create a spurious return.
recommended_action: Switch SP->ES at a quarterly roll, computing the transition-week return within one contract family.
verification: Stage 2: transition-week futures return vs SPX return difference < 0.5%.

finding: The SP chain contains contracts that never traded to maturity: all carry LAST_TRADEABLE_DT = 2021-09-17 (delisting date) and several have single-digit-year tickers.
classification: verified metadata issue (Bloomberg records delisting date as LTD)
why_it_matters: A mapping rule based on 'k-th unexpired contract by LTD' sees 12 contracts tied on one date in mid-2021.
risk_if_ignored: Generic-to-contract mapping becomes ambiguous for SP in Jun-Sep 2021.
recommended_action: Exclude SP contracts with LTD 2021-09-17 from mapping; end SP usage at or before the SPU21 expiry.
verification: Mapping unit test over 2021-06..2021-09.

finding: ES3 is very sparse before late 2007.
evidence: ES3 Wednesdays missing 518 (34.4%); max gap 1092 days ending 2001-03-16.
classification: potentially genuine (third quarterly E-mini barely traded)
why_it_matters: ES3 is only needed to cover early-roll windows.
risk_if_ignored: Early-roll logic that needs ES3 would fail or use stale prices before 2007.
recommended_action: Do not rely on ES3 before 2008; for the S&P a 'first day of contract month' roll needs only generic 2.
verification: Stage 2 check that no return uses an ES3 price before 2008.

finding: SPX is the price index (no dividends) while futures prices embed expected dividends.
evidence: median ES1/SPX 1.0003; yearly medians 0.997-1.006 track rates minus dividend yield.
classification: verified definition; consistent with paper ('S&P 500 Composite')
why_it_matters: Carry creates a small predictable basis drift.
risk_if_ignored: Minor; a total-return spot would change the mean hedged return only.
recommended_action: Keep SPX; document.
verification: n/a

finding: The LBMA Gold PM file used by the paper has a header and no observations.
classification: verified data gap
why_it_matters: The paper's spot is the London PM fix; XAU is a different fixing time and source.
risk_if_ignored: Undisclosed substitution of the paper's spot series; small timing basis differences vs COMEX settlement.
recommended_action: Use XAU Curncy and state the deviation; if possible pull LBMA PM from another source for a 1990-2023 robustness check.
verification: Correlation of weekly XAU vs LBMA returns if obtained.

finding: The GC calendar lists all 12 months, but generics roll only through active months (G,J,M,Q,V,Z).
evidence: roll test share of LTDs followed by G2/G1 spread jump: cycle months 0.878 (3d/5x: 0.937); off-cycle months 0.186 (3d/5x: 0.552)
classification: verified statistically (consistent with context doc claim)
why_it_matters: Mapping generics to contracts with all months included would mis-identify the held contract half the time.
risk_if_ignored: Spurious roll returns and wrong 'first day of contract month' roll dates.
recommended_action: Filter GC calendar to active months before mapping.
verification: Stage 2 mapping test: implied rolls align with spread jumps.

finding: Gold fell ~9-11% in one day (XAU -9.0%, GC1 -11.4%).
classification: potentially genuine market event (corroborated by independent spot and all three generics)
why_it_matters: Largest daily gold move in the sample; inside the 2023-2026 extension window.
risk_if_ignored: Treating it as an outlier and removing it would understate gold tail risk.
recommended_action: Keep; mention in the extension discussion.
verification: n/a

finding: XAU (Bloomberg composite) and COMEX settlement are sampled at different times; on volatile days spot sits above the front future.
classification: reasonable interpretation (timing, not error)
why_it_matters: Timing differences show up as basis noise.
risk_if_ignored: Slightly understates hedge effectiveness for all models; affects naive and OLS similarly.
recommended_action: Accept and disclose.
verification: n/a

finding: Futures generics have a price on Friday 2017-12-15, before CME bitcoin futures began trading (trade date 2017-12-18). The calendar's earliest contract is BTCF18.
classification: unresolved (pre-launch indicative or misdated print)
why_it_matters: Affects at most the first weekly return.
risk_if_ignored: A spurious first futures return in a 9-year sample.
recommended_action: Start the BTC futures sample on the first Wednesday on/after 2017-12-18 (2017-12-20).
verification: Assert first futures date >= 2017-12-18.

finding: BRR includes weekend values through 2022, almost none in 2023-2025, and some again in 2026.
classification: unresolved (likely pull/calendar artifact; BRR is published daily)
why_it_matters: No effect on Wednesday sampling (0 missing Wednesdays).
risk_if_ignored: Only matters if daily data are used.
recommended_action: Ignore for weekly work; document.
verification: n/a

category: large uncorroborated move on a Wednesday
finding: BRR fell ~25% on Wednesday 2018-01-17 and recovered the next day, while XBTUSD and BTC1 moved little over the same interval.
classification: potentially genuine (BRR's 4pm-London fixing caught the intraday crash low of 17-Jan-2018; other series close hours later) but unresolved
why_it_matters: A single Wednesday spot print ~15% below futures sits in the first 52-week Bitcoin estimation window.
risk_if_ignored: Inflates estimated BTC basis risk and tail dependence in the first windows; makes Dec-2018+ hedge ratios depend on one timing artifact.
recommended_action: Keep BRR as primary (it is the CME settlement reference) but run the BTC analysis with XBTUSD spot as sensitivity.
verification: Stage 2: list weekly BRR-vs-BTC1 basis outliers; compare hedge ratios under both spot series.

finding: Daily BTC1/BRR ratio has wide tails, e.g. 2019-06-26/27 when bitcoin crashed intraday.
classification: reasonable interpretation: BRR fixes at 4pm London, CME settles ~4pm New York, so crashes between the two show up as basis
why_it_matters: This is a central H2 mechanism: measured basis risk partly reflects timing, not economics.
risk_if_ignored: Attributing timing basis to 'unstable spot-futures relation' over-states the H2 story.
recommended_action: Keep; in Stage 2 compare weekly spot-futures correlation using BRR vs XBTUSD as a timing sensitivity.
verification: Correlation table with both spot series.

finding: Bloomberg Henry Hub spot printed 0.2571 for one day.
classification: verified data error (likely decimal shift; contradicted by FRED and futures)
why_it_matters: A Monday, so it does not enter strict Wednesday sampling, but would enter any daily statistic or fallback.
risk_if_ignored: A fake -240% / +250% log move in daily diagnostics or in a fallback week.
recommended_action: Treat as missing in Stage-2 processing via an explicit, documented exclusion list (raw file untouched).
verification: Exclusion list applied; processed series has no |daily log change| > 1 without corroboration.

finding: Bloomberg Henry Hub has no prints during the peak of Winter Storm Uri, including Wednesday 2021-02-17; FRED has them.
classification: verified coverage gap (the spike itself is a genuine market event)
why_it_matters: Uri is one of the proposal's named stress windows; the peak is exactly a Wednesday.
risk_if_ignored: A fallback rule would use 02-12 (6.51) and the stress-window analysis would miss the 23.86 spike, understating spot tail risk and basis risk.
recommended_action: Decision needed: (a) patch missing Bloomberg days with FRED values (median FRED/Bloomberg ratio ~1.000) under a documented rule, or (b) keep Bloomberg only and report Uri with FRED as a side analysis.
verification: Weekly Uri-window table under both options.

finding: Henry Hub spot spikes in Jan-2024 and Jan-2026 while futures move little.
classification: potentially genuine market events (corroborated by two independent spot sources); size differs by source
why_it_matters: These are exactly the spot-only tail events that make a futures hedge (of any ratio) fail; they will dominate NG CVaR.
risk_if_ignored: Removing them would bias H2 towards the naive hedge; using one source without disclosure makes the NG tail source-dependent.
recommended_action: Keep; report H2 NG tail results with the primary spot and, as sensitivity, the other source for affected weeks.
verification: Sensitivity table of NG 1%/99% CVaR HE under both spot sources.

finding: NG1 has a one-day log change of -0.64 (price -47%) when the squeezed Feb-2026 contract expires and the generic rolls to March.
classification: potentially genuine curve structure; the jump is a generic-roll artifact, not a return
why_it_matters: Shows how large NG roll gaps can be in winter.
risk_if_ignored: An uncorrected generic series would record a -64% 'futures return' and make futures look like a terrible hedge.
recommended_action: Roll-correct in Stage 2 (same-contract returns only).
verification: No weekly futures return spans two contracts.

finding: Bloomberg Henry Hub appears to be dated one trading day late from about Jan-2020 to Apr-2021: it matches FRED's previous-day value and moves with the previous day's futures.
evidence: months where Bloomberg(t) is closer to FRED(t-1) than to FRED(t): 14 of 16 in 2020-01..2021-04 (in 2019 the two are identical: monthly median |log diff| 0.000). Daily-change correlation with NG1 in 2020-01..2021-04: Bloomberg same-day 0.034, prev-day 0.336; FRED same-day 0.308. Control 2017-2019: Bloomberg same-day 0.308. Feb-2021: FRED jumps on 02-11 (6.50), Bloomberg on 02-12 (6.51).
classification: verified inconsistency between sources; attribution to a Bloomberg dating shift is strongly supported by the futures anchor (reasonable interpretation)
why_it_matters: Spot and futures must be observed on the same day for basis and hedged returns to be meaningful; this window contains COVID and Winter Storm Uri, both H2 stress windows.
risk_if_ignored: A one-day lag between spot and futures adds artificial basis noise for ~70 weeks, lowers measured hedge effectiveness for every model and is likely to favour OLS over naive, biasing the H2 natural-gas conclusion.
recommended_action: Decision needed: for Jan-2020..Apr-2021 use FRED DHHNGSP (complete in that window) as the NG spot, or shift Bloomberg back one trading day under a documented rule; report sensitivity either way.
verification: After the fix: correlation of daily spot changes with same-day NG1 in the window is similar to 2017-19 and 2021-23 levels.

finding: Bloomberg Henry Hub is flat at 14.50 for 9 consecutive trading days (2005-09-26..2005-10-06) after Hurricane Rita; FRED is blank on the same days.
evidence: max stale run 9 starting 2005-09-26; Wednesdays affected 2005-09-28, 2005-10-05.
classification: potentially genuine event (Henry Hub/Sabine shut-in) with carried-forward values that are not real trades
why_it_matters: Two Wednesdays with zero spot return followed by a catch-up move.
risk_if_ignored: Artificially low spot volatility then a jump; distorts semivariance and basis in a known stress period.
recommended_action: Flag these weeks; sensitivity with them treated as missing.
verification: Stage 2 flag column; HE with/without.

finding: FRED Henry Hub is mostly blank before 2007.
evidence: 2059 blank rows; 405 Wednesdays missing (26.0%); ~70% of 1997-2006 trading days blank.
classification: verified (file content); whether FRED itself is this sparse is unresolved
why_it_matters: Rules out FRED as primary NG spot before 2007 and therefore a 1997 start.
risk_if_ignored: Proposal's 1997-2026 NG sample cannot be delivered with this file.
recommended_action: Use NGUSHHUB (from 1999-01-04) as primary; change the proposal's NG sample to 1999-2026.
verification: n/a

finding: NG spot-futures basis is wide and time varying (largest of the six markets).
classification: potentially genuine (seasonality, storage, delivery-month mismatch)
why_it_matters: This is the core H2 mechanism; also means the roll convention materially changes NG futures returns.
risk_if_ignored: Mis-specifying the roll would be confounded with genuine basis risk.
recommended_action: Report NG results under the main roll rule and one alternative.
verification: Stage 2 sensitivity.

finding: The last two NGUSHHUB values are identical (2.589).
classification: unresolved (possibly pulled before the 11-09 assessment)
why_it_matters: Outside the last sample Wednesday (2026-11-04).
risk_if_ignored: None for weekly analysis if the sample ends 2026-11-04.
recommended_action: End the sample at 2026-11-04 or earlier.
verification: n/a

finding: CFNAI ends at 2026-09; the series is revised over time, and this is a single (current) vintage.
evidence: last 2026-09-01; April-2020 value -18.36 is an extreme (COVID) observation.

why_it_matters: Regime labels for Oct-Nov 2026 weeks are unavailable; revised data differ from what the paper's authors saw in 2023.
risk_if_ignored: Small differences from the paper's regime split; mislabelled final weeks if forward-filled.
recommended_action: Leave the last weeks unlabelled; note the vintage; assign monthly CFNAI to weeks by calendar month (decision in Stage 2).
verification: Count of weeks per regime vs paper where reported.

finding: USREC marks 4 recessions since 1990 matching NBER dates (FRED convention: month after peak through trough); recent zeros are provisional until NBER rules.

finding: SOXX PX_LAST is unadjusted: a 3-for-1 split on 2024-03-07 and another drop of ~3.4x on 2026-11-05.
